thread:
Priya Nair: FYI scheduling a quick sync on the 'graft' minimized base image cutover. target: staging tomorrow 08:00 PT. need final RBAC + KMS sign policy check.
Diego Ramos: can we avoid cluster-level binds for the baker SA? last time that caused audit noise.
Priya Nair: yep. plan is to replace cluster-admin with Role:image-graft-baker scoped to infra-builds. small patch shown below.
```
# RBAC patch
- kind: ClusterRoleBinding
  roleRef: ClusterRole/cluster-admin
+ kind: RoleBinding
  roleRef: Role/image-graft-baker
  namespace: infra-builds
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: ci-baker
  namespace: infra-builds
```
Olivia Zhang: also ensure the Role doesn't include `secrets:*` broad verbs. minimal permissions only `get`, `list`, `create` for signed-artifacts.
Samira Gupta: add an annotation on the patch so the audit log contains ticket id and operator: `k8s.kit/annotate: SEC-992` — that helps later for forensics.
Priya Nair: adding that. for signing, we've moved to KMS-wrap + cosign hybrid. the key policy must allow `AsymmetricSign` for the CI principal and deny decrypt/encrypt. @Olivia can you verify the key policy snippet?
Olivia Zhang: done. snippet: `allow: principals/ci-service; actions: kms.sign` — principle is the GCP service account for CI. i also added a condition limiting signing to the artifact name prefix `graft-*`.
Diego Ramos: great. on runtime surface: canary will run with nodeSelector `staging=true` and seccomp profile `graft-minimal.json`. we should assert no CAP_SYS_ADMIN and no privileged mode.
Samira Gupta: assert added to rollout job: `assert: container.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == false` + `capabilities.drop contains ALL` in pipeline.
Priya Nair: one vuln note — the new libc-min layer removed /lib/ld-linux.so.2 symlink. some tools rely on it for legacy ELF. not exploitable, but breaks a small healthcheck in ops. we'll include a compatibility shim in the staging canary.
Olivia Zhang: shim in the image or add an init container that recreates the symlink? prefer image-level shim so production behaves the same.
Diego Ramos: init container is faster for patching during rollout. ops can iterate without rebuilding upstream images.
Priya Nair: ops prefers patching the image properly. we'll do image shim + short-lived init workaround if we need to rollback quickly.
Samira Gupta: what is the rollback plan if canary fails with a security-related syscall regression?
Priya Nair: immediate revoke of signing permission + roll back tag to previous signed image. ticket will escalate to oncall sec.
audit-bot: checklist update: [RBAC patch annotated], [KMS key policy approved], [cosign key access restricted], [canary nodes reserved], [seccomp profile uploaded], [vuln triage note: shim planned].
Diego Ramos: i'll run eBPF-based syscall tracing in staging during canary and post a short log excerpt here. will also run a seccomp fuzz harness and attach results.
Olivia Zhang: after Diego posts, i'll validate audit log entries include the `operator` and `ticket` annotations, and that signing calls surface `x-trace-id` header in KMS logs. example signing call we'll use:
```
cosign sign --key kms://projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/graft/cryptoKeys/signer \ 
  --annotations "ticket=SEC-992,operator=priya" \ 
  registry.example.com/graft:sha256-abc123
```
Samira Gupta: looks good. please ensure registry retention and image attestation records are preserved for 90 days per compliance pack.
Priya Nair: noted. i'll link the compliance ticket. plan: Diego posts fuzz results by EOD, Olivia verifies key policy + logs, Samira does final RBAC + audit quick-scan. if green, proceed with staging gate.
Diego Ramos: ack. ping me if you want me to hold canary for an extra 2 hours.
Priya Nair: thanks all. i'll post the staging gate link and ping channel 15m before. :wave:
